blogs.title: Finetuning a 65B Model on a Single Laptop: How QLoRA Broke the Memory Barrier
blogs.description: This blog post explains the core breakthrough of QLoRA: how it enables researchers to use consumer hardware (like a single 48GB GPU) to finetune massive language models (65B parameters) that previously required enterprise-scale clusters. It breaks down the mathematical trick—using Low-Rank Adapters and freezing most weights—to show why full-model finetuning became impossible, but finetuning just the 'adapter' weights makes it feasible.

blogs.title: Quantization It Talks Back: Understanding Why 4-Bit Training Works (and NF4)
blogs.description: A deep dive into the 'Quantization Trainer' problem, where standard K-bit quantization methods usually destroy accuracy during training. This article simplifies the new 'NormalFloat4' (NF4) data type from QLoRA, explaining how it optimally handles normally distributed neural networks without performance loss. It also demystifies 'Double Quantization,' a technique that quantizes the quantization constants themselves to shave off gigabytes of memory.

blogs.title: The New Gold Standard for Chatbots: Meet Guanaco and the Elo Ranking System
blogs.description: An exploration of how QLoRA was used to train the 'Guanaco' family of models, which consistently beat previous open-source models and nearly matched ChatGPT's performance despite being 30% smaller. The post introduces the new evaluation methodology proposed in the paper, comparing human raters against GPT-4 self-evaluation and explaining the Elo rating system used to rank chatbot performance in tournaments.

blogs.title: Beyond Benchmarks: Lessons on Data Quality and Hidden Model Failures from QLoRA
blogs.description: This article shifts focus from raw performance metrics to qualitative insights found in the research. It discusses how data quality trumps dataset size, highlights why 'MMLU' scores don't always predict good chatbot behavior, and provides real-world examples of where quantized models fail (such as math problems or theory of mind) to offer a balanced view of current AI capabilities.
